model.name: DORA Critical Functions and ICT Third-Party Map (starter)
model.documentation: Maps critical or important functions to the ICT services that support them and the ICT third-party providers behind those services, alongside the five areas of the Digital Operational Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, applicable since 17 January 2025. The function-to-service-to-provider chain is the backbone of the register of information on contractual arrangements (Article 28(3)) and of exit planning (Article 28(8)). Behind each provider sit the subcontractors that effectively underpin its service, ranked as the register's ICT service supply chain template (B_05.02 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956) asks. This model is a structuring aid, not legal advice.

element.name: Digital operational resilience
element.documentation: The ability to build, assure and review operational integrity and reliability by ensuring the full range of ICT capabilities needed to address the security of network and information systems.

element.name: ICT risk management
element.documentation: Chapter II, Articles 5 to 16: an ICT risk-management framework owned by the management body, covering identification, protection, detection, response, recovery, learning and communication.

element.name: ICT incident management, classification and reporting
element.documentation: Chapter III, Articles 17 to 23: a management process for ICT-related incidents, classification by the set criteria and reporting of major incidents to the competent authority.

element.name: Digital operational resilience testing
element.documentation: Chapter IV, Articles 24 to 27: a risk-based testing programme, with threat-led penetration testing at least every three years for entities the competent authority identifies.

element.name: ICT third-party risk management
element.documentation: Chapter V, Articles 28 to 44: third-party risk strategy, the register of information, pre-contract due diligence, mandatory contractual provisions and exit strategies.

element.name: Information sharing
element.documentation: Chapter VI, Article 45: voluntary arrangements to share cyber threat information and intelligence.

element.name: Register of information (Article 28(3))
element.documentation: A register, at entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated level, of all contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services provided by ICT third-party service providers, distinguishing those that support critical or important functions.

element.name: Exit strategies (Article 28(8))
element.documentation: Exit strategies for ICT services supporting critical or important functions, tested and documented in exit plans.

element.name: Payments processing
element.documentation: Critical or important function: its disruption would materially impair financial performance or the continuity of services.

element.name: Customer account servicing
element.documentation: Critical or important function.

element.name: Regulatory reporting
element.documentation: Important function: supports compliance with authorisation conditions.

element.name: Payments software vendor
element.documentation: ICT third-party service provider, rank 1 in its ICT service supply chain.

element.name: Managed payments service
element.documentation: ICT service provided by the third party.

element.name: Managed payments service agreement
element.documentation: Contractual arrangement recorded in the register of information. Check the mandatory provisions of Article 30.

element.name: Cloud infrastructure provider
element.documentation: ICT third-party service provider, rank 1 in its ICT service supply chain.

element.name: Cloud hosting
element.documentation: ICT service provided by the third party.

element.name: Cloud hosting agreement
element.documentation: Contractual arrangement recorded in the register of information. Check the mandatory provisions of Article 30.

element.name: Payments hosting provider
element.documentation: ICT subcontractor. Hosts the payments software vendor's managed service. Record the date the provider last confirmed this subcontracting arrangement.

element.name: Managed hosting
element.documentation: ICT service delivered by the subcontractor.

element.name: Network connectivity provider
element.documentation: ICT subcontractor. Carries traffic between the payments software vendor and the payment schemes. Record the date the provider last confirmed this subcontracting arrangement.

element.name: Network connectivity
element.documentation: ICT service delivered by the subcontractor.

element.name: Managed security monitoring provider
element.documentation: ICT subcontractor. Runs round-the-clock security monitoring for the cloud infrastructure provider. Record the date the provider last confirmed this subcontracting arrangement.

property.value: Medium complexity in terms of substitutability

element.name: Security monitoring
element.documentation: ICT service delivered by the subcontractor.

element.name: Data centre operator
element.documentation: ICT subcontractor. Operates the data centres used by both the cloud infrastructure provider and the payments hosting provider: a concentration that neither direct contract shows. Record the date the provider last confirmed this subcontracting arrangement.

element.name: Data centre colocation

view.name: Critical functions and ICT third parties
view.documentation: Read top to bottom: a critical or important function, the applications that serve it, the ICT services they run on, and the third-party provider and contract behind each service. Every chain that ends in a single provider with no tested exit plan is a concentration risk to report.

view.name: ICT subcontracting chain
view.documentation: Read top to bottom: a critical or important function, the applications that serve it, the provider's ICT service and contract, the rank 1 provider, and the subcontractors behind it with the services they deliver. The data centre operator serves both chains, at rank 2 behind the cloud infrastructure provider and rank 3 behind the payments software vendor: a concentration the direct contracts do not show.

view.name: DORA requirement areas
view.documentation: The five areas of the regulation, with the two third-party duties this model's map feeds directly.
